transcript:
Meeting Header: 2026-04-05 | 08:30 PT | Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (CSM), Diego Alvarez (SE) -- Polaris: Maya Chen (VP ML), Ethan Ross (Platform), Sara Ibrahim (Privacy), Liam Park (SRE), Noah Patel (CTO), Olivia Green (PM)

Summary:
Quick QBR/check-in focused on an unexpected cost spike in March, tail latency incidents during batch writes, and planning next steps for dedicated capacity & compliance artifacts. Agreed to run targeted benchmarks and share detailed cost breakdowns.

Topics Covered:
- March usage and cost anomaly analysis
- Latency tail vs P90/P99 behavior on long sequences (8k, 16k)
- KV/prefix caching effectiveness and batching tradeoffs
- Dedicated vs hosted capacity for peak daytime traffic
- Compliance artifacts: SOC2 scoping, data residency, KMS options
- Next steps and pilot scoping for dedicated pool

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll keep this tight. agenda: quick cost story, latency, and next steps.
[00:18] Maya: yeah thanks, we have a bunch of stakeholders on, want to make sure we cover the spike and what's realistic w dedicated.
[00:35] Ethan: quick context, our tokens jumped about 45% last month, not sure if it's model change or replay. we also saw p99 jump a lot during morning window.
[01:05] Jordan: okay; do you know if that was foreground inference or async batch reranking?
[01:12] Olivia: mostly foreground, a new recommendation route (rec-gen) that we rolled a week before.
[01:27] Priya: understood. we'll pull per-route delta but initial guess is increased sequence length plus lower cache hits.
[02:00] Diego: on the latency front, if you're going from 8k to 16k tokens, the kernel selection and kv-cache become huge factors; we saw similar patterns with Red Wood Optima on our side where quantization helped but cache misses blow up cost.
[02:28] Maya: "Red Wood Optima"? you mean Redwood Optimize?
[02:32] Diego: yes yes sorry, my bad. the transcriber sometimes splits names.
[03:05] Liam: also saw a few infra retries we had to stitch with our sidecar; may be increasing apparent token counts because of duplicate sends.
[04:10] Jordan: good point, Liam. can you share spike logs and a sample request distribution?
[04:18] Liam: will do, I'll pull last 7 days around the roll-out.
[05:00] Noah: on the compliance side, Sara will be owning the SOC2 conversation but we need to confirm data residency for EU traffic.
[05:10] Sara: yes, EU customers mandate data at rest in eu-west and we'll need KMS integration notes.
[05:40] Priya: we have a private deployment playbook and KMS patterns; i'll attach our whitepaper.
[06:05] Ethan: curious on the dedicated capacity option — what's the delta in baseline cost vs hosted per-token cost?
[06:18] Jordan: dedicated is more of a committed monthly for GPU pools; unit economics usually improve for predictable high throughput but you trade flexibility. we'll send an apples-to-apples per-route baseline.
[07:05] Maya: we have a seasonal peak in June and expect a new product feature launch; might need burst capacity too, not just committed.
[07:22] Diego: Redwood Dedicated supports burst policies and can fallback to hosted variants, but we should model tail-latency for those fallbacks.
[08:10] Olivia: can you run a canary with the 16k model variant? we want to know real-world error and latency under our traffic.
[08:35] Diego: yes we can provision a canary, run end-to-end traces, and include KV cache hit rates. need a sample payload distribution.
[09:12] Jordan: action: Diego to run head-to-head 8k vs 16k tests and share traces.
[10:00] Ethan: imperfect transcriptions aside, what's your guidance on reducing tokens w/o losing quality? we tried summarization prompts which hurt accuracy.
[10:28] Priya: there are prompt engineering levers and also model quantization profiles; Redwood Optimize (sorry Red Wood earlier) can recommend batching and quantization per-route based on evals.
[11:00] Maya: how confident are you that quantization won't degrade our NLU for rec-gen? we've seen regressions with int8 in another stack.
[11:30] Diego: we treat it conservatively; we run regression evals against your golden prompt set before recommending. if quality regresses above threshold we won't suggest that profile.
[12:05] Olivia: is there an SLA difference for dedicated? our legal wants uptime numbers and escalation paths.
[12:22] Jordan: yes, dedicated comes with SLA guarantees; we'll include the SLA doc and escalation matrix.
[13:00] Sara: and audit logs — we need retention options. any retention limits?
[13:12] Priya: by default hosted logs retain 30 days, enterprise add-ons get longer retention and long-tail audit exports. for private you'll have customer-managed retention.
[14:05] Maya: cost breakdown would help; show us per-route, per-model, and caching effects.
[14:22] Jordan: we'll produce a per-route CSV and an executive one-pager.
[15:05] Ethan: about the spike — could it be replayed requests or unforeseen retries? we added a retry in the client last month.
[15:22] Liam: yep, i think the retry window coincides with the spike. i'll check.
[16:00] Diego: one more technical note: if you increase prefix caching and pin common prompts, hit rates can improve dramatically; that reduces tokens and latency. but it requires alignment on prompt variants.
[17:10] Maya: i can assign a small prompt-canonicalization task to our ML team.
[18:00] Priya: i'll coordinate a short workshop on canonical prompts and cacheable prefixes.
[18:28] Jordan: great. next, dedicated scoping — what throughput numbers should we model?
[18:45] Noah: baseline daytime 250 qps, peak 900 qps for 10 minutes, average payload ~6k tokens, 5% of requests hit 16k.
[19:20] Diego: with those numbers we'll size GPU pool and estimate unit costs; we'll also model fallback latency to hosted.
[20:00] Olivia: also want cost-per-1000-requests at those payloads.
[20:22] Jordan: noted.
[22:00] Maya: any red flags on private deployment? we might need VPC peering and strict egress controls.
[22:18] Priya: private supports VPC and on-prem edge; we'll share the network diagram and ports.
[23:12] Sara: and HSM/KMS options for key management.
[23:25] Diego: we integrate with major KMS providers; for air-gapped we have an on-prem package but that has longer lead times.
[25:00] Ethan: curious on observability — token-level breakout and trace correlation?
[25:12] Jordan: Redwood Console gives token-level cost and per-route latency plus request traces; we can expose sample traces to your SRE.
[26:00] Liam: yes we want tracing hooks into our datadog; do you support that?
[26:10] Diego: we can push traces via OTLP or provide logs to your bucket; we'll include config examples.
[28:00] Jordan: ok recap: we'll send cost breakdown, SOC2 artifacts, and schedule the dedicated scoping.
[28:30] Priya: i'll also send the prompt canonicalization workshop invite for next week.
[29:10] Maya: who owns the benchmark? Diego?
[29:18] Diego: yep i'll run it and attach traces.
[30:00] Jordan: any final questions?
[30:12] Olivia: one more — what's the fallback behavior if dedicated pool is saturated? do you auto-route to hosted?
[30:25] Diego: yes you can configure auto-fallback to a compatible hosted model variant; we recommend canarying that path because of possible latency differentials.
[31:00] Ethan: let's make sure the fallback path's model variant has similar tokenization to avoid subtle token count diffs.
[31:15] Jordan: good call.
[33:00] Maya: all right we're comfortable with the plan. thanks team.
[33:25] Sara: we'll compile the compliance list and share with Priya.
[34:00] Jordan: perfect. thanks everyone. we'll send notes and next actions.
[34:20] -- meeting ended --

Call Recap and Next Steps:
- Redwood to provide per-route cost CSV and executive one-pager (Jordan) by 2026-04-08.
- SE to run 8k vs 16k latency/throughput benchmarks with KV-cache hit metrics and attach traces (Diego) by 2026-04-12.
- CSM to share SOC2/ISO artifacts and private deployment whitepaper (Priya) by 2026-04-09.
- Polaris to send spike logs and retry config (Liam) by 2026-04-07.
- Schedule dedicated capacity scoping session week of 2026-04-13 (Jordan + Liam + Diego).
